jobs.title: Last Bell, 2001
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 21, thin young man with a slouch, three days' stubble, dark hair grown longer; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010; GULLY — aged 22, stocky boy with a round face, easy slouch. WOOD usually wears brown canvas chore coat with a frayed cuff and one mismatched button, hands in its pockets, plain tee, dark jeans. GULLY usually wears backwards blue cap, faded green hoodie, muddy tan work boots. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Two years out: Wood on the far sidewalk at 3:05 with the dog, the bell, the kids, and Gully's flatbed passing with a honk. Gully has the last word through the window; Wood has the one after it. Panel 1: a young man and a small dog on a sidewalk across from a small-town high school with a jagged sound shape at its door, brush-pen black and white (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 2: students pouring out of a school's front doors toward a beach road, brush-pen black and white. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: a flatbed truck passing with a young man's arm out the window and a honk drawn as a small shape, another young man on the sidewalk beyond, brush-pen black and white (in this panel: GULLY, WOOD). Gully says "You're not in there anymore.". Panel 4: a young man watching a truck drive away with a small dog looking up at him, brush-pen black and white (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). Wood says "I know.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23; @barnaby for the character Barnaby.
